output.brief: The new operators are not the cause. Second shift looks worse only because all its VX work runs on Press 5. On Press 5 with Arnholt resin, rejects are about 10% on both shifts, and new and experienced operators perform the same. Press 5 with Quillan resin is about 0.9%, and Press 7 is about 0.8% with either supplier. Arnholt resin arrives wetter, at 0.27–0.33% moisture against a 0.20% limit. Dryer D7 handles that. D5 has a degraded dew point, and the alarm limit was loosened in week 31, so it leaves the resin too wet. Quillan resin starts drier, so D5 got away with it until Arnholt was released. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. Neither Arnholt alone nor D5 alone causes the problem. Please don't discipline the operators, and don't drop Arnholt. This week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the alarm limit, keep Arnholt off D5 until D5 is verified, and check moisture at the press for every lot. Separately, check whether the north annex storage is making Arnholt wetter at the dryer inlet. The evidence can't separate that from supplier moisture, so don't pay for rented space yet. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
